links.outcome: NLP sensitivity for SDoH domains versus research survey reference on local patient data
links.effect: Sensitivity was low: highest for alcohol use (55%); lowest for abuse (5%), drug use (0%), financial constraints (16%). Pipeline aligned more with negative survey responses than patient-reported needs.
links.quote: Sensitivity was higher only for alcohol use (55%); the lowest values were for abuse (5%), drug use (0%), and financial constraints (16%).

links.outcome: Agreement between two survey reference standards
links.effect: The two surveys agreed only modestly, so no single instrument gives definitive ground truth; apparent NLP performance depends on which survey is the comparator.
links.quote: The 2 surveys agreed only modestly with each other, so no single instrument provides a definitive ground truth.

unlisted_practices: Comparing NLP-extracted SDoH against patient-reported survey responses as reference standard
Improving clinical documentation practices to capture social needs

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world validation/performance of a transformer NLP pipeline (SODA) for extracting SDoH from clinical notes compared against patient surveys, without testing a specific deployment safeguard or intervention.
